summary.en: Build a vector that doubles safely and shrinks without repeated resizing.
summary.bn: নিরাপদে দ্বিগুণ হয় এমন vector বানাও, আর ঘন ঘন resize না করে ছোট করো।

notes: These implementations use C17. Compound literals and declarations in loop headers date from C99; C17 does not add automatic memory management.

examples.title: Append through two capacity boundaries
examples.explanationHtml: Capacities are 1, 2, 4, 4 and 8. Only live values print; spare capacity reserves room for later appends.

examples.title: Shrink only after enough deletions
examples.explanationHtml: Removing the first few values leaves capacity at eight. Capacity halves when occupancy reaches one quarter, avoiding resize work on every pop.

examples.title: Use an empty vector and reuse its storage
examples.explanationHtml: An empty pop fails without changing size. After removing 72, the reserved slot can hold 85 without another allocation.

examples.title: Build a vector from input
examples.explanationHtml: Five input marks require capacity eight. realloc can move the block, so append updates the owner before writing the new value.

practice.title: Append a stream of marks
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), then n values (-99..99). Start with no allocation, append each value, and print size, capacity and values using the lesson format.
hints: Allocate one slot for the first append.

practice.title: Pop with an underflow check
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), n values (-99..99), and pop count (0..20). Print Removed: count of successful pops, then show the vector.
hints: An empty pop leaves size unchanged.

practice.title: Append only nonnegative readings
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), then n readings (-99..99). Store only nonnegative readings in a vector; print its size, capacity and values.
hints: A rejected reading must not increase size.

practice.title: Remove all copies of one reading
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), n values (-99..99), then target. Compact values in place; apply pop until size matches survivors, allowing the shrink policy to run. Show the vector.
hints: Move survivors first, then change size through pop.

practice.title: Report spare slots
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), then n values (-99..99). Print Spare: capacity minus size after doubling appends.
hints: Allocated slots and live elements are different counts.

quiz.prompt: Why store realloc’s result in a temporary pointer?
options: Failure must leave the old allocation reachable
realloc always frees old storage on failure
The temporary pointer prevents all copying
quiz.explanation: On failure realloc returns NULL and leaves the old allocation valid. Direct assignment could lose its address.

quiz.prompt: When size equals capacity, what must append do before writing?
options: Write past the final reserved slot
Obtain enough space and update the owner
quiz.explanation: A full vector has no destination slot. Writing first would exceed the allocation.

quiz.prompt: What is one append’s worst-case time when doubling moves n values?
quiz.explanation: The allocator may move the existing block. Amortized O(1) describes a sequence, not every individual append.

quiz.prompt: Why shrink at one quarter rather than immediately below one half?
options: To keep size always equal to capacity
To separate shrink and growth thresholds
quiz.explanation: After halving, occupancy is near one half. Several appends are needed before another growth.

quiz.prompt: What should happen if an optional shrink allocation fails?
options: Keep the old capacity and the successful smaller size
quiz.explanation: The pop already removed an element logically. Keeping spare storage preserves a valid vector.

quiz.prompt: How many live values may show print after size becomes three and capacity eight?
quiz.explanation: Capacity includes unused slots, whose contents should not be treated as live values.

quiz.prompt: What does the small vector’s 1024-slot bound protect?
options: Its doubling arithmetic and supported allocation size
The numerical sum of stored marks
quiz.explanation: This teaching library deliberately limits capacity. A general library needs overflow checks against SIZE_MAX.

quiz.prompt: After five appends from capacity one, which capacity is needed?
quiz.explanation: The full boundaries occur before appends two, three and five. Capacities double through 2,4,8, ending at eight.

quiz.prompt: At quarter occupancy, what capacity follows one shrink from eight?
quiz.explanation: Two live elements equal one quarter of eight, so capacity halves to four while size stays two.

quiz.prompt: How many spare slots remain after nine appends reach capacity sixteen?
quiz.explanation: Capacity minus live size is 16-9=7. Those seven slots are reserved but contain no live elements.

quiz.prompt: After capacity eight shrinks to four at size two, how many appends fit before another growth is required?
quiz.explanation: Sizes three and four use spare slots. The following append finds capacity full and grows.

quiz.prompt: Which saved reference survives a moving vector resize as a usable location description?
options: A raw pointer into the old block
A pointer one past the old allocation
quiz.explanation: An index can be applied to the new owner. A pointer into replaced storage no longer identifies a live element.

keyPoints.en: A vector stores an owner pointer, a live size and a capacity.
keyPoints.bn: Vector-এ মালিক পয়েন্টার, ব্যবহৃত size আর capacity রাখতে হয়।

keyPoints.en: A temporary realloc result preserves the old owner when growth fails.
keyPoints.bn: realloc-এর ফল অস্থায়ী পয়েন্টারে রাখলে ব্যর্থতায় পুরোনো মেমরি হারায় না।

keyPoints.en: Doubling gives constant amortized append time despite occasional linear copying.
keyPoints.bn: দ্বিগুণ করে বাড়ালে মাঝে কপি লাগলেও append-এর amortized খরচ ধ্রুব থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Shrinking at one-quarter occupancy leaves room before the next growth.
keyPoints.bn: এক-চতুর্থাংশ ভরলে ছোট করায় পরের growth-এর আগে ফাঁকা জায়গা থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Pointers into vector storage may become invalid after realloc moves it.
keyPoints.bn: realloc মেমরি সরিয়ে নিলে vector-এর ভেতরের পুরোনো পয়েন্টার আর বৈধ থাকে না।

examQuestions.question: List capacities after appending values 1 through 9 to an empty vector.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The capacities are 1,2,4,4,8,8,8,8,16. Resize copies total 1+2+4+8=15 old elements. Each append also writes one new element.

examQuestions.question: Show why doubling provides O(1) amortized append time.
examQuestions.answerHtml: For n appends, capacities form powers of two. Copied old elements form a geometric sum smaller than 2n. The n new writes plus fewer than 2n copies total O(n), so dividing by n gives O(1) per append over the sequence.

examQuestions.question: Write safe realloc growth for a full bounded vector, explaining failure.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
size_t capacity = vector->capacity == 0 ? 1 : 2 * vector->capacity;
if (capacity > 1024) {
    return 0;
}
int *values = realloc(vector->values, capacity * sizeof *values);
if (values == NULL) {
    return 0;
}
vector->values = values;
vector->capacity = capacity;

The owner changes only after success. Callers must discard saved pointers into the old allocation after a moving resize.

examQuestions.question: Give a grow/shrink policy that avoids resizing on alternating append and pop.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Double only when full. Halve when size is at most one quarter of capacity, keeping at least one slot. After halving, the vector is roughly half full, leaving a gap before the growth boundary. Failed optional shrinking keeps the old storage.
